key_insight: Combining a Bayesian uncertainty-aware coordination layer with an adversarial multi-agent LLM team in a low-code platform yields more reliable, self-checking scientific code generation and evaluation—even when success metrics are ill-defined.
problem_solved: Addresses unreliable LLM-generated scientific workflows by reducing error propagation across chained agents and providing robust evaluation and debugging when domain success metrics are ambiguous.
method: Three LLM-based agents coordinated under a Bayesian framework: a Task Manager that formalizes/decomposes user goals, a Code Agent that generates and iterates on scientific code, and an Adversarial Validator that probes, tests, and challenges outputs to surface faults.
Bayesian belief modeling to represent agent uncertainty and guide when to request rework, escalate checks, or accept solutions—minimizing cascading errors in multi-step workflows.
Low-code Platform (LCP) orchestration that integrates execution, automated tests, and human-in-the-loop touchpoints so non-experts can run, inspect, and refine complex AI-for-Science pipelines.
impact: Enables AI/ML practitioners and domain scientists to auto-generate and validate scientific code with fewer silent failures, faster debugging cycles, and clearer uncertainty signals—accelerating reproducible experimentation.

paper_title: AI-for-Science Low-code Platform with Bayesian Adversarial Multi-Agent Framework
paper_authors: Zihang Zeng, Jiaquan Zhang, Pengze Li, Yuan Qi, Xi Chen
